identification.summary: ELECTRIC PANDA is a CrowdStrike adversary name. CrowdStrike presented it in a 2013 CrowdCasts webinar alongside GIBBERISH PANDA and TEST PANDA [S4]. CrowdStrike uses the PANDA suffix for China-based actors [S5]. In April 2020 the name appeared in a US Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) bulletin reported by Politico [S1][S2].
identification.firstObserved: CrowdStrike CrowdCasts webinar naming the actor: 2013 [S4]. Activity start date is not stated in the sources gathered.
identification.notes: The name is not widely used by other vendors. A report quoted in the Politico coverage says it is not a widely accepted designation for a state-sponsored group [S1]. No source gathered maps ELECTRIC PANDA to a Microsoft name, a MITRE ATT&CK group, or to another vendor's cluster such as APT27 or Emissary Panda. Do not merge it with those clusters.

attribution.sponsor: Chinese government, as attributed by CrowdStrike according to the Politico coverage of the DCSA bulletin [S1]. The name's PANDA suffix is CrowdStrike's convention for China-based actors [S5].
attribution.confidence: The DCSA bulletin, as reported, said activity was from 'highly likely' Electric Panda actors [S1]. This describes confidence that the activity matched the actor, not confidence in state sponsorship. No formal government attribution to a named PRC agency was found.
attribution.basis: CrowdStrike naming [S4][S5]; DCSA bulletin to cleared contractors as relayed by Politico and syndicated coverage [S1][S2]. The underlying bulletin and CrowdStrike technical reporting were not opened.

targeting.notes: Per the DCSA bulletin as relayed by CyberWire summarizing Politico, 38 cleared contractor facilities were targeted since 1 February 2020 and roughly 600 connections were tied to Electric Panda actors; targeted sectors reportedly included health care technology, aerospace, naval and telecommunications [S2]. The search summary of the Politico mirror also notes that detection of both inbound and outbound traffic led one former NSA researcher to speculate US collection on the actor's command-and-control, which is speculation by that expert [S1]. Sector list is from secondary reporting only.

campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike CrowdCasts webinar lists ELECTRIC PANDA with GIBBERISH PANDA and TEST PANDA [S4].

campaigns.name: DCSA bulletin to cleared contractors
campaigns.summary: DCSA warned cleared contractors that 38 facilities had been targeted since 1 February 2020 by actors it tied to Electric Panda, with about 600 connections noted; Politico reported that naming a specific actor in such warnings is unusual [S1][S2].

diamond.adversary: China-based actor named by CrowdStrike; sponsor attributed to the Chinese government per Politico coverage [S1][S5].
diamond.victim: Cleared US defense contractor facilities in health care technology, aerospace, naval and telecommunications, per secondary reporting of the DCSA bulletin [S2].

gaps: No malware, exploits, tradecraft or infrastructure for ELECTRIC PANDA were found in open sources; capabilities and Diamond capability/infrastructure remain empty.
The DCSA bulletin itself and the original Politico article were not opened; findings rest on a seclists.org mirror and a CyberWire summary seen only in search results (page fetches failed).
Any CrowdStrike adversary page were not opened; the 2013 naming is known only from the Malpedia listing and search snippet.
No mapping to Microsoft naming, MITRE ATT&CK or other vendor clusters (including APT27/Emissary Panda) was found; overlap is unverified.
Objectives, activity timeline between 2013 and 2020, and activity after 2020 are unknown.
The 2020 bulletin's 'highly likely' wording and whether the traffic reflects victim compromise or US collection are not independently verified.
